ClassSummary.description: Units in the bag per class, counting only supplied lines. Every field is present; clients omit zeros.

packages.description: Every package the driver was shown at this stop, with its outcome, in one request. Only what is named is settled: an unnamed package stays waiting and the stop stays open (`CollectResponse.remaining`).

collected.description: How many were collected and declared not available by this call.

remaining.description: Packages on the stop this request did not name (added meanwhile); when above 0 the stop stays open and the app re-reads it.

CollectionIssueRequest.description: POST /driver/v1/collection/runs/{runId}/stops/{stopId}/issue: report a missing or short package.

deliveredBy.description: Who takes it from the hub: an Effy driver or a courier.

packageCode.description: The code on this package's label (`EFY1:<code>`): bag 1's.

packageId.description: The package's own id, as `CollectRequest.packages[].packageId` names it.

parcels.description: The package's live bags ("Bag n of N"); every step accounts for every bag.

windowLabel.description: The day and window an Effy parcel is for, in the server's words; null when none.

CollectionStopDTO.description: GET /driver/v1/collection/runs/{runId}/stops/{stopId}: a shop stop and its packages.

opening.description: When this stop's round opens; `null` = open. Collecting is refused before then.

address.description: The shop's address for the device's maps app (never a position). Null when not yet recorded, which back-office readiness reports; the driver is told it is missing.

parcels.description: The stop's live bags, each with its own code ("Bag n of N"), for matching a scan offline.

customerPhone.description: The customer's checkout phone, for calling from the door: sent only while the drop is open and only to the round's own driver; never in history or run lists.

deliveryWindow.description: The window the customer was sold. Due and late are derived by the app from the clock, never sent.

handover.description: How the customer asked for the order to be handed over, or null. A request, not a constraint: the app says it and leads the proof chooser with it, but never removes a way of completing the drop.

instructions.description: The customer's note to the driver, verbatim plain text; null when they wrote none.

loaded.description: The van has been loaded with this drop; until then nothing on it can be done.

opening.description: When this drop's round opens; `null` = open. Every action is refused before then.

window.description: The same window as a ready-made label in Melbourne time ("5 pm – 7 pm"), so the app never formats a time.

completedAt.description: When and how a finished drop was finished: the proof method or the failure reason.

deliveryWindow.description: The same window as instants, so the app can say Due and Late as the clock moves.

parcels.description: The drop's live bags ("Bag n of N"), for matching a scan offline.

street.description: The street line, for the run list ("5 Faraday St"); null when the address has none.

summary.description: The drop's total across its packages, so cold goods show in the list.

window.description: The window as a ready-made label, e.g. "5 pm – 7 pm" (Melbourne time).

deadlineAt.description: The end of the delivery window, or of the day where there is none.

stage.description: The run's stage and its words.

toReturn.description: Parcels from failed drops on this run, still with the driver, to be checked back in at the hub; `null` when none.

DeliveryWindow.description: A delivery window, as two instants.

hubSort.description: Where each package goes at the hub, in the platform's words, so the hub scan can say it offline.

stage.description: The run's stage and its words.

DriverMeDTO.description: GET /driver/v1/me: the record-backed identity. Display strings only.

vehicleCheck.description: Today's pre-trip vehicle check: `due` until answered (no work until then), `unsafe` until a dispatcher clears it, `none` with no vehicle.

zone.description: What the driver is cleared to cover, as one line (Today, Help, Account), derived from their clearances. Null when cleared for nothing, which the app renders as unavailable.

DriverRunType.description: The two kinds of work a driver run can be (back-office reads it too). Work is typed tasks, not roles: one driver often runs a collection round and then a delivery round in a shift.

DriverVehicle.description: What the driver is driving, for their Account screen, read from their open vehicle holding. Both fields are null when they hold no vehicle.

DriverVehicleCheckState.description: The state of the driver's vehicle check today.

state.description: `due` | `ok` | `unsafe` | `none`, a string on the wire; the app treats an unknown value as `ok`.

vehicleLabel.description: "Toyota HiAce · ABC123", for the check screen's title.

DropPackageRef.description: One physical package at a drop, in a stable order the app labels by position ("Package 1 of 2"). A package is one shop's portion, so it carries no shop id, name or code, and never may.

packageCode.description: The code on this package's label (`EFY1:<code>`): bag 1's.

parcels.description: The package's live bags ("Bag n of N"); every step accounts for every bag.

to.description: `out_for_delivery` is written only by loading the van.

acknowledgeHeldPackages.description: "I have seen what I am carrying and I am going off duty anyway." Going off duty with packages in the van is refused (409, naming every package) until this is set: a shift cannot end silently on goods.

expectedEndAt.description: When the driver expects to finish, if they say; absence means unknown. Never defaulted to a shift length: a guess would decide someone's workload as if it were a fact.
null: the driver did not say. Render as "unknown", never as a time.

HandoverMethod.description: How a package was handed over: scanned from its label, its code typed (a torn label), or ticked by hand.

HandoverPreference.description: Delivery instructions: how to hand the order over, and a short note. The vocabulary, the length limit and the normalisation rule live here only; the customer surfaces use them for a remaining-characters count and checkout calls `normaliseDeliveryInstructions` itself, so client and server agree. `delivery-instructions.fixtures.json` is the rule's table of cases.

failureReason.description: Why a drop came back to the hub.

map.description: A run's map (every stop done), and its window in words.

packageCount.description: A drop's packages, and the window it was sold.

stops.description: For a run: its stops in order, each with how it ended. Absent for a drop.

failureReason.description: Set for a drop that was not delivered (its parcels went back to the hub).

street.description: The street line, how it was handed over, and for a drop that came back, why.

packageCount.description: Packages on the run, and a delivery run's window in words.

HistoryStop.description: One stop of a finished run, as History lists it. No money, no customer name.

failureReason.description: Why a drop came back to the hub.

title.description: The shop's name, the drop's street and suburb, or "Hub check-in".

HubCheckinEffyGroup.description: The Effy parcels of one check-in that wait for one day and window.

anyTime.description: Sold a day with no time.

date.description: yyyy-mm-dd (Melbourne) of the window; null for a parcel sold no window.

dueToday.description: True when these go out today (loaded for a delivery round); false means shelved for a later day. Decided by the server.

courierCount.description: Parcels a courier takes from the hub.

effyCount.description: Parcels Effy delivers, in all and by the day and window each waits for; the driver classifies nothing. `label` is written by the server ("Today, 4 pm – 6 pm"). A parcel sold no window has null instants.

held.description: Packages declared not in the van at this check-in, now held for dispatch.

nextCourierPickupLabel.description: When the courier next collects from the hub, in the server's words; null when no courier parcel or no service.

HubSortInstruction.description: One package's hub instruction. `label` is the whole line: "LOAD NOW · Today 4–6 pm".

kind.description: `load_now` | `shelve` | `courier_bay` (`HubSortKind`), a string on the wire so a new kind cannot break the read; an unknown kind shows the label.

parcelCodes.description: Every bag of this package: each scanned at the hub gets this instruction.

LabelReadDTO.description: One read as the client made and judged it. `clientReadId` makes an offline replay record once; `deviceAt` is when it happened on the device, kept however late it arrives.

LoadRequest.description: POST /driver/v1/delivery/runs/{runId}/load: the van is loaded; every staged drop goes out.

held.description: Packages taken off the run as not loaded, and drops removed because nothing was left.

loaded.description: How many drops this call moved to out for delivery.

LoadStep.description: "Load the van": the run, and what goes in it.

included.description: False when the shop supplied none of this line. Shown as "not included", never hidden.

qty.description: The quantity in the bag: what the shop gathered (less than `orderedQty` when part-supplied, 0 when not supplied).

ParcelDTO.description: A live parcel as every surface sees it. `of` = this package's live bags.

ParcelMissingReason.description: Why a bag was not handed over at a step. `other` needs a note.

returned.description: How many parcels this call returned; 0 when nothing was left to return.

roundComplete.description: True when the run is now finished.

ParcelsToReturn.description: What a driver still has to bring back to the hub from a delivery run's failed drops.

orders.description: Order numbers only: no address, no customer.

parcels.description: Each parcel for the Return to hub screen: its ref, where it was for and why it came back.

ParcelsUnaccountedProblem.description: The 409 when a live bag was neither handed over nor declared missing.

ProblemFieldIssue.description: RFC 9457 problem+json: the platform's one machine-readable error shape.

field.description: The offending field path, or for a whole-request refusal a stable machine-readable code (e.g. `cap_below_floor`, `bands_required`), so the client can say which rule was broken.

code.description: A stable refusal code where the route defines one (e.g. `slot_required`), mapped by the client to its own copy; `detail` is prose.

parcels.description: Every bag of the drop, handed over or declared missing (`ParcelStepFields`).

ReadMethod.description: How a read was made. A bag ticked by hand is not a read: it is a hand-over with method `manual`.

ReadOutcome.description: What a read means, everywhere. `not_found` is decided by the server only.

parcels.description: The package's live bags ("Bag n of N"); every step accounts for every bag.

RoundOpening.description: When a round opens. Sent only for a round not yet open (the server judges by its own clock), so a wrong phone clock cannot lock an open round.

at.description: The instant, ISO 8601, which the app's clock is compared with to unlock by itself.

label.description: The same moment in words, Melbourne time. The app never formats a time.

hub.description: The hub's point, where "Navigate to the hub" goes.

stops.description: In route order: a collection run ends at the hub, a delivery run starts there.

RunMapPoint.description: The run map, decorative: where a run's stops roughly are, for a small schematic. A stop's point is its postcode's place (never a geocoded address or a device position); the hub's is its own. Nothing that orders or assigns work reads it. Stops with no point are left out.

n.description: The stop's number in the run's list; null for the hub.

TemperatureClass.description: How an item must be carried, in the driver's words (the catalogue's `ambient` is shown "Normal").

changedNote.description: What dispatch changed on the current round while under way ("Added 2 drops"); null when nothing. Shown until dismissed.

deadlineAt.description: The current round's deadline; `null` only with no current round.

dueLabel.description: The deadline in words, Melbourne time ("2 pm", "tomorrow 11 am").

loadStep.description: The current run is an open delivery run not yet loaded: loading is next, `active` is null, and no drop can be done before it.

opening.description: When the current round opens; `null` means open (or none). Work is assigned as soon as a driver can take it; its actions are refused until it opens (409 `round_not_open`, with `opensAt` and `opensLabel` as field issues).

progress.description: Progress through the current round, and its map.

stage.description: The current run's stage (`RunStage`) and its words ("Collecting 2 of 5").

toReturn.description: The current round's parcels still to return to the hub; when that is all that is left, `active` is null and this is shown.

upcoming.description: The driver's other unfinished rounds, soonest first.

TodayItemRef.description: A compact reference to the active or queued work item on the home. `hub_checkin` keeps a finished collection round reachable until it is checked in.

coldCount.description: Packages holding chilled or frozen goods.

street.description:
What the Today card and its "Up next" rows show:
- `street`: a drop's street line ("12 Lygon St"), the card's title; null for a shop or the hub.
- `place`: the rest in one line, a shop's full address or a drop's "Carlton VIC 3053".

window.description: A drop's window, in the server's words, and its instants (for "Due now" / "Late").

TodayProgress.description: How far through the current round the driver is. Counts only.

packagesInVan.description: Collection: packages picked up so far / still to pick up.

UpcomingRound.description: A round the driver holds besides the current one.

VehicleCheckItem.description: The six things a driver checks before taking the vehicle out.

WireInt.description: A whole number on the wire. A plain `number` becomes a Kotlin `Double` and sends `1.0`; this makes the schema say `"integer"` (a Kotlin `Long`). Use it for every count, quantity, limit and revision.

description: Codegen entry only. Every field forces a type into the schema.
title: DriverContract
